commits.patch:
diff --git a/lib/parsedate.c b/lib/parsedate.c
index 9630a988b9..98437f31bf 100644
--- a/lib/parsedate.c
+++ b/lib/parsedate.c
@@ -125,7 +125,6 @@ static const int16_t tzone[] = {
   -7 * 60,            /* Golf */
   -8 * 60,            /* Hotel */
   -9 * 60,            /* India */
-  -1,                 /* J - not a timezone */
   -10 * 60,           /* Kilo */
   -11 * 60,           /* Lima */
   -12 * 60,           /* Mike */

coupling: The defect is an out-of-bounds read of the single-letter time zone table lib/parsedate.c:tzone[] reached from the public API curl_getdate() with a perfectly ordinary RFC 1123 date whose zone is the military letter 'Z' (\"Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 Z\"). It only exists when the two edited commits are composed; each one, on its own, is internally consistent and benign. Commit a9eeb8d3f2 ('parsedate: find day names, months and time zones faster') drops the dead placeholder entry for the letter J from the alpha-sorted table - J is not a time zone and is rejected before lookup, so the entry was unreachable - and correspondingly shifts the lookup index to tzone[check[0] - 'A' - (check[0] > 'J')] so letters K..Z still hit the right slots in the now 25-entry table. That commit is correct: every index it computes is in bounds (verified by building that tree alone: the PoC parses cleanly, rc 0). The later commit 791f5e19d7 ('parsedate: time zone strings') rewrites checktz(): it hoists first = check[0], converts the table to a plain int16_t array, and re-derives the lookup as the canonical upstream expression tzone[first - 'A'] * 60 - silently discarding the slot-skip that commit one had added, because that expression is exactly what the original 26-entry table used. Read alone, neither diff is wrong: commit one removes a dead entry and keeps its own index aligned; commit two's diff relative to the real upstream commit is a single table line (no J slot carried forward, a natural consequence of its parent) and its index line is byte-identical to upstream. Only their combination is buggy: a 25-entry (50 byte) global indexed with first - 'A', so 'Z' (and only 'Z') reads tzone[25] - two bytes past the object - which AddressSanitizer reports as a global-buffer-overflow in checktz (letters K..Y merely read a neighbouring zone's offset, silently wrong). A correct fix cannot come from either commit's diff alone: reverting commit one's index shift still leaves the 25-entry table from commit one upstream of commit two's rewrite, and patching only commit two's table requires knowing commit one deliberately removed the J slot. The fix has to reconcile the table layout introduced in commit one with the index expression introduced in commit two - restore a placeholder slot or restore the slot-skip - which is reasoning across both commits.
